newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria assures UK army rule will end next year.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria assures UK army rule will end next year.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Tuesday told former colonial power Britain that it would hand over power to an elected president next year.
An official statement said Nigeria's number two, Lieutenant-General Oladipo Dipo, gave the assurance when he received Britain's new high commissioner (ambassador) Graham Burton in the capital Abuja.

Diya said the government was satisfied with the implementation of its transition to democracy programme and deliberate measures were being put in place to ensure it ended on October 1, 1998, with the installation of a democratically elected government.

Britain's new labour government has taken a much harder line against Nigeria than its conservative predecessor. Foreign Secretary Robin Cook last week accused the military government of corruption, saying it should remain suspended from the Commonwealth for lack of democracy and human rights abuses.
Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in November 1995 for executing writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight minority rights activists despite widespread appeals for clemency.
In May, Nigeria told the labour government not to damage the "special relationship" between the countries but has made no formal response to Cook's latest stinging comments on Nigeria.
Diya asked the ambassador to work hard to improve Anglo-Nigerian relations which he said were "currently at a low ebb as a result of misunderstanding".
He said "minor adjustments" to the transition timetable would not affect the 1998 terminal date of the administration.
Burton, who arrived in May, has over the past several weeks met senior Nigerian officials, including military ruler General Sani Abacha in Abuja.
The West imposed sanctions on Nigeria for annulling a 1993 poll meant to restore democracy.
